title: Multi-Modality Multi-Attribute Contrastive Pre-Training for Image Aesthetics Computing
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: In the Image Aesthetics Computing (IAC) field, most prior methods leveraged the off-the-shelf backbones pre-trained on the large-scale ImageNet database. While these pre-trained backbones have achieved notable success, they often overemphasize object-level semantics and fail to capture the high-level concepts of image aesthetics, which may only achieve suboptimal performances. To tackle this long-neglected problem, we propose a multi-modality multi-attribute contrastive pre-training framework, targeting at constructing an alternative to ImageNet-based pre-training for IAC. Specifically, the proposed framework consists of two main aspects. 1) We build a multi-attribute image description database with human feedback, leveraging the competent image understanding capability of the multi-modality large language model to generate rich aesthetic descriptions. 2) To better adapt models to aesthetic computing tasks, we integrate the image-based visual features with the attribute-based text features, and map the integrated features into different embedding spaces, based on which the multi-attribute contrastive learning is proposed for obtaining more comprehensive aesthetic representation. To alleviate the distribution shift encountered when transitioning from the general visual domain to the aesthetic domain, we further propose a semantic affinity loss to restrain the content information and enhance model generalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework sets new state-of-the-arts for IAC tasks.

title: NHANES-GCP: Leveraging the Google Cloud Platform and BigQuery ML for reproducible machine learning with data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
venue: arXiv (Cornell University)
abstract: Summary: NHANES, the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, is a program of studies led by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) designed to assess the health and nutritional status of adults and children in the United States (U.S.). NHANES data is frequently used by biostatisticians and clinical scientists to study health trends across the U.S., but every analysis requires extensive data management and cleaning before use and this repetitive data engineering collectively costs valuable research time and decreases the reproducibility of analyses. Here, we introduce NHANES-GCP, a Cloud Development Kit for Terraform (CDKTF) Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and Data Build Tool (dbt) resources built on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) that automates the data engineering and management aspects of working with NHANES data. With current GCP pricing, NHANES-GCP costs less than $2 to run and less than $15/yr of ongoing costs for hosting the NHANES data, all while providing researchers with clean data tables that can readily be integrated for large-scale analyses. We provide examples of leveraging BigQuery ML to carry out the process of selecting data, integrating data, training machine learning and statistical models, and generating results all from a single SQL-like query. NHANES-GCP is designed to enhance the reproducibility of analyses and create a well-engineered NHANES data resource for statistics, machine learning, and fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs). Availability and implementation" NHANES-GCP is available at https://github.com/In-Vivo-Group/NHANES-GCP

title: Opening thoughts from the new Editors
venue: Journal of Product Innovation Management
abstract: On January 1, 2025, we started our 3-year term as the new co-Editors-in-Chief (co-EiCs) of the Journal of Product Innovation Management (JPIM). Launched in 1984, JPIM is now the world's premier innovation management journal. Since its inception, JPIM has been owned by a professional association (the Product Development and Management Association—PDMA), and supported by a global community of innovation management scholars and practitioners. As a team, we have our common roots in this community, which we have served and supported in various capacities over time. We are now excited to lead JPIM through the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead. We are grateful to the previous editors, Jelena Spanjol, who has been at the helm for two consecutive terms (2019–2024), Charles Noble (2019–2023), and Gloria Barczak (2023–2024). The professionalism, dedication, and passion with which they have served JPIM and its community certainly set a high bar for us. As the previous editors recall in the last “From the Editors” essay (Spanjol, Noble, & Barczak, 2024), they reconfigured the editorial structure and process and introduced several new initiatives including Catalyst articles, a trailblazer Reviewer Development Program (RDP), Paper Development Workshops (PDWs) for prospective authors, and a redesign of the journal's visual style. JPIM's impact factor increased from 3.78 in 2018 to 10.1 in 2024 under their leadership, with the contribution of world-class authors, associate editors (AEs), and reviewers. We are particularly grateful for the generous time and resources that Jelena and Gloria have committed to assisting us through the editorial transition in the last months. Their knowledge, support, and advice were invaluable. To ensure continuity, Jelena and Gloria will handle all manuscripts that were in process as of December 31, 2024, and will see through manuscripts that they had previously assigned to one of the AEs from their team until a final decision is reached. In the remainder of this editorial, we will: (1) set our vision for the role of JPIM given the current grand challenges; (2) describe our editorial structure and process; (3) share our strategy and new initiatives to sustain JPIM's impact and growth; (4) introduce important new guidelines on Generative AI and data sharing; and (5) present our plans for engagement and dissemination of JPIM articles within and beyond academia. As we write this essay, the future and prosperity of communities in every corner of the earth are threatened by a series of severe and interconnected grand challenges: wars, climate change, poverty, health, well-being, and social crises. Mitigating or reversing their negative consequences requires innovations in products, technologies, business models, organizational forms, systems, and policies. As JPIM editors, we cannot ignore the role of innovation management (research) in the collective effort to enable current and future generations and the natural environment to survive and thrive. Crossing disciplinary boundaries has been part of JPIM's DNA from the very beginning.1 We are loyal to this vision and want to reaffirm JPIM's position as the home for interdisciplinary and collaborative research between social scientists, engineers, computer scientists, health scientists, and natural scientists focused on common innovation management problems that matter to society. JPIM is driving the field by defining new and forward-looking paths for innovation management research such as ‘liquid’ innovation, the implications of Generative AI for innovation management (research), the prevalence of sustainable business model innovation, and the growing need to break away from the traditional profit-driven market-value logics to embrace new forms of responsible and public value innovation (Spanjol, Noble, Baer, et al., 2024; Spanjol, Noble, & Barczak, 2024). In summary, our mission is to continue strengthening JPIM's position as a global top-tier research journal for cutting-edge, interdisciplinary, socially impactful, and ethically conducted research in the field of innovation management. As a team of co-EiCs, we will work closely together and share the same duties and responsibilities. We believe that the strength of the JPIM community lies in the rich diversity of its members' expertise, backgrounds, and skills. We reflect this diversity in the unique composition of the Co-EiCs team, which, for the first time in JPIM history, is distributed across three continents. In keeping with this value, we made a deliberate effort to assemble a gender-balanced team of AEs, which consists of 22 distinguished innovation management researchers, representing different geographies (Asia, Australasia, Europe, North America), disciplines (e.g., design, entrepreneurship, marketing, management, organization, strategy, technology), backgrounds, world views, research philosophies, and methodological orientations. We will have two dedicated AEs for our RDP, which will continue to offer a route for early career innovation scholars from around the world to join the community as reviewers. We thank all our AEs for stepping into this role and look forward to working with this remarkable group of colleagues. We also reviewed the composition of the Editorial Review Board (ERB) to ensure a balanced representation of the JPIM community and the right mix of expertise. The full list of JPIM editorial roles is available on the journal's website. We maintained the review process workflow introduced by Spanjol and Noble during their first term as JPIM editors (see Figure 1). Specifically, we will oversee desk rejections, allocation of reviewers, and straight rejection decisions after the first round of reviews. We will assign promising manuscripts to one of the AEs, who will process the paper from that point onward, making a recommendation to us at every iteration of the review process. While maintaining the existing review process workflow, we aim to shorten the review cycle by reducing the time for major revisions from 6 to 4 months and minor revisions from 4 to 2 months. This will improve the “time to market” for JPIM articles, which we see as very important for an innovation management journal. As a norm, we aim to reach a final decision within two review rounds. Following the practice of the previous editors, editorial support for JPIM will be co-located with one of the Co-EiCs at Cardiff University. We sincerely thank Zuzana Schneiderova for her excellent work and dedication over the last 6 years. We aim to sustain the growth trajectory JPIM followed over the last four decades. High-impact factors are the result of high-quality manuscripts being cited by a wide range of scholars. In this section, we focus on our new initiatives to attract high-quality manuscripts to the journal. We cover the important issue of dissemination later in the essay. The first route to nurture and attract high-quality research will be to invest time and resources in organizing and running more PDWs. PDWs have already been hosted by previous editors; we will intensify this activity by working with our AEs, leading innovation scholars, conference organizers, other journal editors, and institutions to host more PDWs in different parts of the world. We strategically selected AEs who can add value to the review process with their expert guidance, while simultaneously acting as boundary spanners between the journal and a range of academic communities. We plan to achieve this through several types of events, such as co-hosting PDWs in partnership with AEs respective institutions. We have identified potential hosts in the US, Europe, Asia, and Australasia and will be announcing a roadmap for PDWs events later in 2025. To support these efforts, we will complement the pool of AEs and ERB members by establishing an Advisory Board comprising a small group of highly accomplished scholars and practitioners, who will provide insights and advice on strategic issues and future directions. These Advisory Board members will also assist us in our efforts to further promote the journal among academics and practitioners. As a further way to attract high-quality research, we will continue to actively support the JPIM Research Forum and IPDMC conference, which are the core annual events for our community and an important source for JPIM's pipeline. There will be dedicated ‘Special Sections’ in JPIM attached to these two conferences. To tap into new and emerging talents, we will also continue to support the PDMA Doctoral Consortium, PDMA Doctoral Dissertation Proposal Competition, and IPDMC Doctoral Workshop. In addition, we plan to leverage our geographical distribution to actively represent JPIM in other key conferences and forums where innovation management work is presented and debated. We will continue to welcome Special Issue (SI) proposals on emerging topics to increase JPIM's impact on the field. Emerging topics are increasingly dynamic and often involve cross-disciplinary collaboration. We welcome innovation management research topics that particularly address grand challenges and the unique future research directions highlighted by Spanjol, Noble, Baer, et al. (2024). We retain the SI proposal submission process introduced by previous editors and aim to publish two topical SIs annually. As a significant innovation in JPIM's manuscript portfolio, we introduce a new article category: JPIM Review. JPIM Review will be a regular section within JPIM featuring articles that provide a synthesis and critical appraisal of a particular research stream within innovation management, next to highlighting important directions for future research inquiries and distilling implications for managerial practice. Proposals for JPIM Review articles should be submitted to the EiCs, who will decide whether to invite the author(s) to develop the proposal into a full manuscript. This new category of articles will replace Virtual Issues. Unlike Virtual Issues, JPIM Review articles will provide a synthesis of relevant research that goes beyond articles published in JPIM. We will reposition the Catalyst category by emphasizing the novelty dimension. Going forward, this article category will be a regular section of JPIM dedicated fully to essays intended to spark and catalyze new thinking. We are specifically interested in novel interpretive reflections and prospections from both academics and practitioners on a variety of innovation management themes and methods. This category aims to publish essays that are interesting and provocative and do not necessarily conform to conventional wisdom. Hence, JPIM Catalyst articles seek to generate new debates and discussions on innovation management. The essays can be subjective in nature but should be rooted in experience or past scholarship. Proposals for JPIM Catalyst articles should be submitted to the EiCs, who will decide whether to invite the author(s) to develop the proposal into a full manuscript. In recent times, there have been mounting concerns within the research community about dishonest and unethical practices, such as paper mills, inappropriate use of Generative AI to produce manuscripts, and lack of transparency and rigor in data collection and analysis. We will be highly vigilant about these issues. As a first step, we introduce additional and more specific guidelines on the use of Generative AI and data-sharing requirements. The current position of JPIM in relation to the use of AI by Authors is as follows (Spanjol & Noble, 2023): (1) Authorship: JPIM does not permit generative AI technologies and tools to be listed as authors on submissions. (2) Disclosure: If authors use generative AI technologies in preparing a manuscript, JPIM requires a disclosure statement (see below) to be included within the cover letter and a dedicated appendix (to be used for editorial and review purposes and which may be published online upon acceptance). The dedicated appendix should include information such as prompts provided to LLMs, output generated and used, etc., and be uploaded as a separate document into the submission system. JPIM follows Wiley's policy to exclude the reporting of tools and technologies (including services provided by human editors) used “to improve spelling, grammar, and general editing”. Disclosure Statement “In preparing this manuscript, the author(s) used the following [GENERATIVE AI TECHNOLOGIES/TOOLS] in order to [REASON/S]. The specific content generated by these AI technologies/tools in the manuscript is clearly marked and described in a dedicated appendix, to be used for editorial and review purposes. Prior to submission, the author(s) reviewed the content generated and take(s) full responsibility for the content of the submitted manuscript.” To these guidelines, we added an explicit statement about the use of generative AI by editors and reviewers, which was absent in the previous version. Our guidelines for reviewers and editors are based on Wiley's guidelines on publication ethics (https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html#22): The peer review process is a human endeavor and responsibility and accountability for submitting a peer review report, in line with a journal's editorial polices and peer review model, sits with those individuals who have accepted an invitation from a journal to undertake the peer review of a submitted manuscript. This process should not be delegated to a GenAI tool. Editors or peer reviewers should not upload manuscripts (or any parts of manuscripts including figures and tables) into GenAI tools or services. GenAI tools may be used only on a limited basis in connection with peer review. A GenAI tool can be used by an editor or peer reviewer to improve the quality of the written feedback in a peer review report. This use must be transparently declared upon submission of the peer review report to the manuscript's handling editor. We also want to formalize JPIM's expectations regarding data-sharing and transparency. So far, like other comparator journals, JPIM has encouraged data sharing but has not produced a set of specific guidelines on the matter. Building on the Transparency Openness Promotion (TOP) guidelines and Wiley's data-sharing policy, as of January 1, 2025, we adopted the following guidelines: JPIM will publish papers where authors indicate whether the data, methods used in the analysis and materials used to conduct the research will be made available to any researcher for purposes of reproducing the results or replicating the procedure. Authors must, in a specific data availability statement, indicate if they will or will not make their data, analytic methods, and study materials available to other researchers. If an author agrees to make materials available, the author must specify where that material will be available. The above guidelines correspond to Level 1 of the TOP guidelines (https://osf.io/9f6gx/wiki/Guidelines/) and Wiley's “Expect Data Sharing” policy (https://authorservices.wiley.com/author-resources/Journal-Authors/open-access/data-sharing-citation/data-sharing-policy.html). In essence, data sharing is optional, but the inclusion of a data availability statement is mandatory. The authors of accepted manuscripts will be required to provide a “data availability statement” that confirms the presence or absence of shared data. Data sharing includes but is not limited to raw data, processed data, software, algorithms, protocols, methods, and materials. If data are shared, the authors must provide details about the data repository used. A selection of data availability statement templates and suitable data repositories will be available for the authors of accepted papers. We are aware that the landscape of Generative AI and data transparency in the academic publication sector will change as technology evolves and new policies are developed. We believe that no journal can take a strong stance in isolation from others; therefore, we will seek to cooperate with editors and publishers of comparable journals to keep JPIM abreast of these developments. We will also work with the PDMA Publications Committee and our Advisory Board to turn these guidelines into formal policies in due course. To promote JPIM content to our key audiences and break through the increasing volume of academic publications that compete for attention, we strategically focus on a series of opportunities. First, we will continue to leverage the resources and opportunities provided by PDMA, which owns JPIM. Specifically, JPIM will be a platform for dialogue between academic researchers, practitioners, and policymakers via its articles, the JPIM's annual research forum, and other innovation conferences and events that bring these different communities together. We will continue to promote articles via PDMA/JPIM's official channels and take further advantage of other formats (e.g., podcasts and videos) to appeal to a wider scope of audience. Likewise, we will encourage and support authors who want to go the extra mile and disseminate the findings of their published research through mainstream channels (e.g., theconversation.com, industry and policy outlets, and digital media). Finally, we will engage highly visible thought leaders among practitioners and policymakers in a dialogue with the journal (through written contributions and digital media), as well as encourage non-academic experts to write Catalyst articles (see above), sharing their thought-provoking insights related to innovation management. For all of the above initiatives, we will benefit from the insights and advice of our AEs and Advisory Board members. A journal is only as good as the community of people who constitute it. As Co-EiCs of JPIM, we want to have a positive impact on the journal itself and on the environment within which it operates. In the words of JPIM's founder Tom Hustad, “By working together we can create a future where we are even more proud of what we are responsible for having accomplished than we now are” (Hustad, 2013, p. 91). We are grateful for the opportunity and support (past, present, and future) provided by the JPIM community. We look forward to publishing original research that advances the field of innovation management, benefits educators and students, influences practice, and helps make the world a better place. title: Optimizing Service Deployments With NLP Based Infrastructure Code Generation - An Automation Framework
abstract: In this paper we discuss how we combine natural language processing (NLP) techniques and infrastructure as code (IaC) tools like Terraform; to build a framework that converts natural language queries into Terraform code, enabling users to generate multi-cloud infrastructure configurations. We detail the construction of the NLP engine, the implementation for benchmarking various context-aware models, and the validation and execution of code, which leads to the integration of the model with DevSecOps pipelines. For benchmarking, we test models such as RoBERTa, GPT-4, T5 and Llama on their performance in terms of accuracy, latency and capacity to translate complex infrastructure requirements given as conversational queries into deployable terraform configuration. On one hand, this framework enhances the accessibility and efficiency of writing Terraform code (TF-code), while on the other, it results in a 73% reduction in the overall time required to bring a service from development to production deployment, relative to comparable efforts performed through manual processes. This modularity allows the entire framework to be customized and integrated into larger systems, especially in a DevSecOps context where flexibility and extensibility are crucial. Finally, the paper provides both technical insights and practical benchmarks, offering a comprehensive solution for organizations seeking to optimize cloud service deployment pipelines using advanced NLP techniques.

title: Realizing Intent-Driven Network Management with TM Forum Standards
venue: IEEE International Workshop on Computer Aided Modeling and Design of Communication Links and Networks (CAMAD)
abstract: This paper details the realization of Intent-driven Management with TM Forum standards. As networks become more autonomous, a key challenge is balancing customer needs with network and resource operations. Intent-based networking (IBN) offers a solution by abstracting service expectations and implementation complexities. We propose an architecture for IBN that follows the TM Forum Intent representation generated using LLMs. The architecture includes the Service Intent Manager, Network-Compute Fabric, and Resource Infrastructure, each playing a critical role in transforming natural language business requests into actionable network tasks. We implemented this architecture and tested it by orchestrating video streaming services on a Kubernetes platform. The results demonstrate how IBN architecture supports the seamless translation of user intents into network operations, enabling autonomous network management and enhancing service provision across diverse domains.

title: Repairing Infrastructure-as-Code using Large Language Models
venue: IEEE Secure Development Conference (SecDev)
abstract: Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) is the practice of provisioning and managing cloud resources using machine-readable code. IaC is seeing increased adoption because it enhances transparency and reliability of infrastructure operations. However, as any software code, IaC can also contain misconfigurations, which can lead to insecure infrastructure, which may result in data breaches. Existing IaC scanning tools are able to detect common misconfigurations in IaC but they require IaC developers to manually repair the code. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have led to promising results in applying LLMs to Automatic Program Repair (APR) tasks for code written in different languages. In this work, we propose an LLM-based approach to fix misconfigurations in IaC code. After misconfigurations in IaC code are identified by scanning tools, we feed the LLMs with the IaC code, details about the misconfigurations, and additional context provided by a human-in-the-loop and prompt the LLM to generate the repaired IaC code. We tested our approach on several vulnerable IaC repositories and found that the GPT-4 model from OpenAI suggests fixes that reduce up to 84.7% of the misconfiguration alarms produced by the scanners and our two-pass solution significantly improves the performance over a one-pass only approach. However, of the fixes suggested, we manually determined that only 79.6% actually solve the problem, while the remaining 20.4% are hallucinated fixes. Specifically, LLM hallucinations in the generated outputs pass checks for misconfigurations but fail other syntax and schema validation checks or do not address the underlying security issue. We propose a few potential approaches to tackle this challenge.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation on Hybrid Cloud: A New Architecture for Knowledge Base Systems
venue: IIAI International Congress on Advanced Applied Informatics (IIAI-AAI)
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a novel approach that combines the strengths of large language models and external documents to generate responses grounded in retrieved information. This technique is particularly useful for building knowledge base systems. However, deploying such systems requires a large amount of computational resources for hosting language models, and keep privacy of the document is also a concern. Through the nature of hybrid cloud, the knowledge base system can maintain data privacy while benefiting from the scalability of public clouds. This study leverages a hybrid cloud architecture, and utilizes Kubernetes as a cloud orchestrator to schedule the workload across different cloud environments. The implemented RAG system demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed architecture, showcasing enhanced privacy, flexibility, and security.

title: Securing AI-Assisted Cloud Engineering: Guardrails For Copilot-Generated IaC And CI/CD Changes To Prevent Vulnerability Injection
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The quick pace of AI coding assistant adoption in cloud engineering has greatly led to the creation of Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and CI/CD pipelines. Nevertheless, AI-generated setting may readily imply security misconfigurations, insecure defaults and violations of the policy that can be transmitted straight into production cloud environments. Such risks are especially acute in those organizations that deal with regulated and high-assurance industries, whose misconfigured resources can cause data breaches, privilege increases, and violation of the rules. Conventional security review procedures are too sluggish and manual to follow through with the AI-assisted development processes, which resulted in a pressing need of automated preventive security mechanisms. The paper presents a recommendation in the form of the AI Guardrailed Cloud Engineering Framework (AGCEF) that is a proactive security model that involves the imposition of guardrails on AI-generated IaC and CI/CD artifacts prior to the deployment. AGCEF combines policy-as-code checking, matching of vulnerability signatures, semantic intent checking with LLM and a quantitative risk scoring system, which identifies and thwart insecure configurations at design time. Through experimental analysis, it is shown that AGCEF is significantly better in comparison to current AI-based methods of vulnerability detection because it offers higher vulnerability prevention, lowers false negatives, less manual review, and enhances the safety of deployment. The framework allows organizations to use AI copilots to enhance productivity and maintain high levels of cloud security and compliance, hence restoring the balance between the speed of AI-assisted development and AI-assisted operations in the cloud.

title: Towards a Reliable Offline Personal AI Assistant for Long Duration Spaceflight
abstract: As humanity prepares for new missions to the Moon and Mars, astronauts will need to operate with greater autonomy, given the communication delays that make real-time support from Earth difficult. For instance, messages between Mars and Earth can take up to 24 minutes, making quick responses impossible. This limitation poses a challenge for astronauts who must rely on in-situ tools to access the large volume of data from spacecraft sensors, rovers, and satellites, data that is often fragmented and difficult to use. To bridge this gap, systems like the Mars Exploration Telemetry-Driven Information System (METIS) are being developed. METIS is an AI assistant designed to handle routine tasks, monitor spacecraft systems, and detect anomalies, all while reducing the reliance on mission control. Current Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) Models, while powerful, struggle in safety-critical environments. They can generate plausible but incorrect responses, a phenomenon known as "hallucination," which could endanger astronauts. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes enhancing systems like METIS by integrating GPTs, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Knowledge Graphs (KGs), and Augmented Reality (AR). The idea is to allow astronauts to interact with their data more intuitively, using natural language queries and visualizing real-time information through AR. KGs will be used to easily access live telemetry and multimodal data, ensuring that astronauts have the right information at the right time. By combining AI, KGs, and AR, this new system will empower astronauts to work more autonomously, safely, and efficiently during future space missions.

title: Using a Feedback Loop for LLM-based Infrastructure as Code Generation
venue: arXiv (Cornell University)
abstract: Code generation with Large Language Models (LLMs) has helped to increase software developer productivity in coding tasks, but has yet to have significant impact on the tasks of software developers that surround this code. In particular, the challenge of infrastructure management remains an open question. We investigate the ability of an LLM agent to construct infrastructure using the Infrastructure as Code (IaC) paradigm. We particularly investigate the use of a feedback loop that returns errors and warnings on the generated IaC to allow the LLM agent to improve the code. We find that, for each iteration of the loop, its effectiveness decreases exponentially until it plateaus at a certain point and becomes ineffective.
ta_note: feedback loop for LLM-based IaC generation

title: A Comprehensive Survey on AI-Enabled Cloud Security, DevSecOps, and Scalable Digital Infrastructure
venue: Preprints.org
abstract: The survey thoroughly discusses the meta splicing of AI, cloud computing, DevSecOps and Cyber security and their successful application on digital infrastructure of contemporary age. It explores implementation of scalable cloud-native architectures, adoption of DevSecOps into CI/CD pipelines as well as use of AI in threat detection, compliance monitoring, and as part of secure software delivery. The paper also presents an increasing area of research in the form of generative AI for synthetic data generation, AI-powered fraud detection in financial systems, Kubernetes-based multi-cloud orchestration, zero trust security for distributed environments. It is a domain focused systematic literature review that looks at domain specific applications such as SAP, ERP systems and synthesizes results from different research works. The report offers insights into current approaches, new technologies and future directions to enable agility, security and intelligence across enterprise-level computing environments.

title: A Framework for Intent-Driven Kubernetes Configuration Generation Using Large Language Models

title: A machine learning-based framework to support monoliths to microservices migration: from identification to packaging and deployment
venue: Espace ÉTS (ETS)
abstract: The migration from monolithic to microservices has gained significant attention due to the growing demand for scalable, maintainable, and agile software systems. While microservices offer benefits, such as independent deployment, fault isolation, and enhanced scalability,migrating an existing monolithic system is a complex, resource-intensive, and error-prone process. This process involves multiple interdependent phases: pre-migration, service identification, service packaging, deployment, and monitoring, each presenting distinct challenges. Existing migration approaches rely heavily on expert-driven, manual techniques, making the process costly, time-consuming, and error-prone. Recent advancements in Machine Learning and Large Language Models provide new capabilities for analysing source code, learning patterns from existing systems, and generating code or configurations, thus offering concrete opportunities to automate and optimise the migration process. While some phases, such as service identification, have been extensively studied, others, such as microservice packaging and deployment configuration, remain underexplored and require substantial manual effort. This thesis begins with a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) of 81 primary studies on machine learning-based approaches to monolith-to-microservices migration, published between 2015 and 2024. The SLR provides a comprehensive analysis of existing techniques and reveals that, while service identification has been extensively studied, the phases of microservice packaging and deployment configuration remain underexplored and largely reliant on manual effort. Building on these findings, this thesis introduces a machine learning-driven framework that automates the three key phases of the migration process, identification, packaging, and deployment, thereby reducing manual effort and enabling the transition toward a modular and cohesive microservices architecture. The framework comprises the following ML-based approaches: (1) Service Identification via MicroMiner, which leverages clustering and semantic analysis to decompose monolithic systems into microservices aligned with single-responsibility and bounded context principles; (2) Service Packaging via MicroPacker, which employs LLM-guided transformation to modularise code, generate standardised APIs, and integrate foundational microservice patterns; and (3) Service Deployment via MiDKo, which applies retrieval-augmented generation to automatically produce accurate Kubernetes and Docker configurations. Collectively, these contributions minimise manual intervention, enhance the architectural quality and modularity of the resulting microservices, and ensure the generation of valid deployment artifacts, resulting in cohesive and deployable microservices ready for execution in modern cloud environments.

title: A Multi-Agent Coding Assistant for Cloud-Native Development: From Requirements to Deployable Microservices
venue: International Conference on Computer Science and Management Technology (ICCSMT)
abstract: The rapid adoption of cloud-native architectures has created an urgent demand for automated development tools that can translate natural language requirements into deployable cloud-native microservices. While recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled AI-assisted code generation, existing approaches predominantly focus on isolated code completion tasks rather than end-to-end software delivery. This paper presents CloudMAS, a multi-agent coding assistant framework that orchestrates specialized agents to transform user requirements into deployable cloud-native applications. Our system comprises six specialized agents: an Architect Agent for service decomposition and API design, three parallel Coder Agents specialized in backend, frontend, and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) generation respectively, a Tester Agent for automated test synthesis and execution, and an Ops Agent for container configuration and Kubernetes manifest generation. These agents are coordinated by a dedicated Orchestrator Agent that manages workflow execution and conflict resolution. We introduce a novel conflict resolution mechanism that enables agents to iteratively refine outputs through structured feedback loops. To address the lack of systematic benchmarks for end-to-end cloud-native development, we construct CloudDevBench, a publicly available evaluation dataset containing 50 real-world development tasks with associated test suites and deployment validation criteria. Experimental results demonstrate that CloudMAS achieves 92% compilation success, 81% test pass rate, and 84% deployment success rate, substantially outperforming single-LLM and single-agent baselines across all metrics.

title: A Review of Generative AI and DevOps Pipelines: CI/CD, Agentic Automation, MLOps Integration, and LLMs
venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Computer Science & Technology
abstract: This paper provides an overview of recent advancements and discussions surrounding Generative AI and its intersection with DevOps practices, leveraging a collection of contemporary research and articles. The increasing adoption of AI agents and machine learning models is transforming various aspects of software development and operations. This paper presents a comprehensive review of Generative AI applications in DevOps automation, covering 50 key research works published between 2023-2025. We analyze the transformative impact of AI-driven solutions across the software development lifecycle, including code generation, infrastructure management, continuous integration/delivery, and Kubernetes operations. The convergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI), intelligent agents, and automation is revolutionizing DevOps and cloud-native software engineering. This paper provides a comprehensive review of how generative AI and agentic workflows are transforming the development, deployment, and operation of modern software systems. We examine the integration of AI-driven automation in continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, the adoption of cloud-native technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes, and the emergence of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and progressive delivery models. The study highlights the benefits of these advancements, including increased efficiency, enhanced reliability, and accelerated innovation, while also addressing the challenges of security, compliance, observability, and skill development. By synthesizing insights from recent research and industry practice, this paper identifies the top terms, theories, and algorithms shaping the field and offers a forward-looking perspective on the evolution of AI-driven DevOps through 2029. The findings aim to guide researchers, practitioners, and organizations in leveraging the transformative potential of intelligent automation for resilient and adaptive software engineering. The review systematically examines how generative AI enhances deployment efficiency, monitoring capabilities, and overall development workflows while addressing challenges in cloud-native environments. Our analysis reveals emerging trends in AI agents for DevOps, containerized AI solutions, and the integration of large language models with existing DevOps toolchains.

title: A Review on AI-Assisted Automation Process for OS Building and Deployment
abstract: Operating System (OS) installation and deployment traditionally require specialised domain expertise and extensive manual effort. Traditional OS installation can be time-consuming, error-prone, and requires manual decision-making. AI-assisted Operating System (OS) installation is an emerging interdisciplinary field that blends artificial intelligence (AI), system automation, and software engineering to streamline and optimize the process of build and deploying operating systems. With AI integration one aims to improve accuracy, efficiency, adaptability, and scalability in various environments, from personal computing to enterprise-level deployments. This paper presents an up to date survey for AI-driven framework that automates the design, configuration, compilation, testing, and deployment of typically used operating systems, eg. Ubuntu, and Debian. Leveraging large language models (LLMs), reinforcement learning, and DevOps automation pipelines, the system intelligently interprets user requirements to produce specifications according to project requirements, then dynamically generates configuration template for used in automated OS installation, test and validate, and eventually fine-tuned to generate an optimized OS. Analysis and review shows significant reductions in development time, improved consistency, and higher adaptability across various hardware and cloud environments. This work highlights the transformative potential of AI in Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for AI for infrastructure management segment, and proposes some approach and techniques for improvise autonomous OS installation and deployment process.

title: A Survey of Textual Adversarial Attacks and Defenses on Large Language Models (LLMs)
venue: Science and Technology of Engineering Chemistry and Environmental Protection
abstract: The broad use of large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 and LLaMA in dialogue systems, content generation, etc., causes security flaws of these models to rise. The current study examines progress made in recent years on textual adversarial attacks and defenses for LLMs, focusing on special attack vectors and defensive techniques targeting LLMs. Firstly, a 'Target—Technology—Scenario' three-dimensional attack classification framework that mainly consists of typical kinds of attacks including PIA and JBA. Secondly, defense mechanisms from two different perspectives: alignment enhancement in the training phase and security controls in the inference phase. In addition, by conducting experiments using benchmark datasets (HELM), existing technical drawbacks and future work directions are also discussed. The aim is to offer guidance and references for subsequent work on theoretical studies of LLM security and promoting the building of stronger NLP systems.

title: A Survey on Task Scheduling in Carbon-Aware Container Orchestration
venue: arXiv (Cornell University)
abstract: The soaring energy demands of large-scale software ecosystems and cloud data centers, accelerated by the intensive training and deployment of large language models, have driven energy consumption and carbon footprint to unprecedented levels. In response, both industry and academia are increasing efforts to reduce the carbon emissions associated with cloud computing through more efficient task scheduling and infrastructure orchestration. In this work, we present a systematic review of various Kubernetes scheduling strategies, categorizing them into hardware-centric and software-centric, annotating each with its sustainability objectives, and grouping them according to the algorithms they use. We propose a comprehensive taxonomy for cloud task scheduling studies, with a particular focus on the environmental sustainability aspect. We analyze emerging research trends and open challenges, and our findings provide critical insight into the design of sustainable scheduling solutions for next-generation cloud computing systems.

title: A14 Transforming combat casualty care training: generative AI-enabled adaptive learning in forward medical settings
venue: BMJ Military Health
abstract: Background NATO leaders have identified the rapid training of military and civilian first responders to deliver far-forward combat casualty care in austere, resource-limited environments during Large-Scale Combat Operations (LSCOs) as a key priority. Variability in baseline learning aptitudes complicates the achievement of this objective. Adaptive learning systems use algorithms to analyse a learner’s performance and customize educational content to meet individual learners’ needs, accommodating for differences in learning styles, and baseline aptitudes. Question-and-Answer (QA) set creation is essential to adaptive learning systems but is highly resource-intensive. Question-and-answer set creation is hindered by the limited availability of subject matter experts, high production costs, and extended delivery timelines. Objectives We describe how we leveraged generative artificial intelligence techniques to rapidly and cost- effectively generate high-quality medical QA sets consistent with National Board of Medical Examiners (NBME) standards. We analysed and described the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs ) as authors of medical QA sets and judges of QA set quality, using a human Subject Matter Expert (SME) as the gold standard. Methods A medical SME rated OpenAI model (GPT-4, GPT-4o, o1-mini, and o1) performance on 320 LLM-generated medical QA sets using a three-tier scale: ‘High’ for complete task coverage, ‘Medium’ for minor omissions, and ‘Low’ for critical omissions. Subsequently, four LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, and o1) served as judges and rated 417 QA sets using standardized judging prompts. Individual LLM performance and the interrater agreement across all four LLMs and human SME were calculated. Results When provided access to reference content, a human SME required approximately 24 minutes to author 1 high-quality medical QA set at an estimated cost of $100 USD. In contrast, each large LLM generated an individual medical QA set in roughly 20 seconds at a fraction of the cost (0.98 cents per QA set). Among the LLMs, GPT-4o emerged as the most effective author, producing high-quality medical QA sets in 86.6% of instances, medium-quality sets in 9.8%, and low-quality sets in 3.7%. The SME agreed with the high-quality ratings of QA sets by GPT-4o 87.4% of the time. The interrater agreement between the human SME and LLMs serving as judges of QA set quality was robust (Krippendorff’s alpha value of 0.85). Conclusions This study documented that LLMs can generate and evaluate high-quality medical QA sets with an estimated 31-fold reduction in time and 4,444-fold reduction in cost compared to those authored by human SMEs as illustrated in the accompanying figure 1. Large language models, when utilized as both authors and judges, with continued human oversight for quality control, can address challenges like limited availability of SMEs, as well as time and cost constraints, thereby enhancing the scalability of adaptive learning and potentially revolutionizing medical training. Future efforts involve creating customized training for first responders (e.g., appropriate use of limb tourniquets) in LSCOs by mapping QA set generation to curricular objectives within an adaptive multimodal learning system. The selected system will need to account for compromised network infrastructure (e.g., offline capability, caching, or minimal bandwidth solutions). title: ACSE-Eval: Can LLMs threat model real-world cloud infrastructure?
venue: Lecture notes in computer science
abstract: While Large Language Models have shown promise in cybersecurity applications, their effectiveness in identifying security threats within cloud deployments remains unexplored. This paper introduces AWS Cloud Security Engineering Eval, a novel dataset for evaluating LLMs cloud security threat modeling capabilities. ACSE-Eval contains 100 production grade AWS deployment scenarios, each featuring detailed architectural specifications, Infrastructure as Code implementations, documented security vulnerabilities, and associated threat modeling parameters. Our dataset enables systemic assessment of LLMs abilities to identify security risks, analyze attack vectors, and propose mitigation strategies in cloud environments. Our evaluations on ACSE-Eval demonstrate that GPT 4.1 and Gemini 2.5 Pro excel at threat identification, with Gemini 2.5 Pro performing optimally in 0-shot scenarios and GPT 4.1 showing superior results in few-shot settings. While GPT 4.1 maintains a slight overall performance advantage, Claude 3.7 Sonnet generates the most semantically sophisticated threat models but struggles with threat categorization and generalization. To promote reproducibility and advance research in automated cybersecurity threat analysis, we open-source our dataset, evaluation metrics, and methodologies.

title: Aduvia: A Multi-Purpose AI-Powered Learning Management System (LMS)
venue: Novel Intelligent and Leading Emerging Sciences Conference (NILES)
abstract: Modern educational environments require unified, intelligent platforms that integrate conversational assistance, formative assessment, and secure exam management. We present Aduvia, an AI-driven system built on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and the Llama 3.3 large language model, which delivers subject-specific, context-aware dialogue; automated quiz generation with instant feedback. Our methodology comprises five phases: (1) content Processing via OCR and semantic chunking, (2) embedding using the e5-base-v2 model and FAISS indexing, (3) RAG-based retrieval with dynamic prompt engineering and context management, (4) generative inference on a GPU-scaled Kubernetes cluster with responsive streaming, and (5) microservices deployment with comprehensive monitoring and iterative feedback loops. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that Llama 3.3 reduces non-streaming response latency by ∼0.4 s and streaming latency by 30–40% compared to version 3.0. Embedding comparisons show that e5-base-v2 produces tighter similarity distributions (0.50–0.93) versus MiniLM (0.27–0.83). A relevance classification threshold of 0.65 yields a precision of 0.85, recall of 0.92, and F1 score of 0.88. These results validate Aduvia’s capability to enhance engagement, accuracy and operational efficiency in digital learning.

title: Adversarial Hallucination Engineering: Targeted Misdirection Attacks Against LLM Powered Security Operations Centers
venue: Preprints.org
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in Security Operations Centers (SOCs) for alert triage and threat‑intelligence synthesis. We study Adversarial Hallucination Engineering (AHE): attacks that bias LLM reasoning by introducing small clusters of poisoned context into retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, producing targeted fabrications aligned with attacker goals. Using a safe, fully synthetic simulator of a RAG+LLM SOC, we formalize the AHE threat model, introduce Hallucination Propagation Chains (HPCs)—mutually reinforcing poisoned documents designed to create artificial consensus at retrieval time—and evaluate a lightweight defense, Chain‑of‑Thought Attestation (CoTA), based on per‑token uncertainty, provenance attribution, and source reputation. Across three model scales, hallucination‑induction rate (HIR) rises superlinearly with HPC size (e.g., for a Large‑70B proxy, 12.45%→61.84% as HPC size in top‑k grows 0→5); actionable misconfiguration rate (AMR) grows from 3.23% (no attack) to 38.18% (HPC‑5). CoTA reduces attack‑success rate (ASR) by ~55% for HPCs≥3 at ~7% false‑positive flags and ~8% latency overhead. We release synthetic artifacts to support reproducible, defensive research.

title: Agentic AI Framework for Multi-Cloud DevSecOps Automation and Software Supply Chain Security
venue: International Journal of Recent Advances in Science and Technology
abstract: The rapid adoption of multi-cloud environments has transformed software development and deployment practices, creating complex challenges in DevSecOps automation, security governance, and software supply chain protection. Traditional DevSecOps approaches often depend on rule-based automation, fragmented security tools, and human-driven decision-making, which limits scalability and responsiveness against emerging cyber threats. This research proposes an Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework designed to enhance multi-cloud DevSecOps automation and strengthen software supply chain security through autonomous, intelligent, and adaptive agents. The proposed framework integrates AI-driven agents capable of continuous monitoring, threat detection, policy enforcement, vulnerability management, compliance assessment, and automated remediation across heterogeneous cloud platforms.The framework combines machine learning, large language models, security orchestration, infrastructure-as-code validation, and supply chain intelligence to create a proactive security ecosystem. Agentic AI enables autonomous reasoning, collaboration among specialized agents, and dynamic decision-making throughout the software development lifecycle. The research methodology adopts a design science research approach involving framework development, architecture modeling, and evaluation through security automation scenarios. The proposed model aims to reduce operational complexity, improve threat response time, and enhance visibility across distributed cloud environments. The study contributes an intelligent DevSecOps paradigm that supports secure, resilient, and automated software delivery pipelines.

title: Agentic Penetration Testing using Secure Shell: Context-Aware Command Generation and Analysis Using Open-Source LLMs
abstract: Penetration testing (also known as Pentesting) is a systematic process that involves the identification and exploitation of vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and potential weaknesses in networks, applications, or hardware to assess their resilience against adverserial threats. Manual penetration testing requires extensive time and effort to identify and exploit vulnerabilities across complex and evolving systems. By generating precise and context-specific commands, Large Language Models (LLMs) can significantly enhance both speed and accuracy of penetration testing. This paper presents an agentic feedback-loop driven framework that involves open-source LLMs (e.g., CodeGemma, CodeLlama, Mistral) to generate linux shell commands for a wide range of penetration testing tasks and to provide an analysis on the lines of vulnerability assessment, explanation and the next recommended steps. The devised agentic framework connects to the target system via Secure Shell (SSH) protocol. The LLM then analyzes the natural language prompt entered by the user and generates a command to be executed on the target system. The console output on the target machine is then again fed to the LLM to provide a detailed analysis. Connecting to the target system via SSH for penetration testing offers several advantages, including secure, encrypted communication and the ability to perform tests without exposing sensitive data over the network. The paper also provides a detailed comparison between various open-source LLMs in their ability to generate various pentesting commands. CodeGemma:7b-instruct demonstrated the highest performance in command generation, achieving an average fuzz score of 62.32. To validate the effectiveness of the framework when integrated with this model, penetration testing was conducted on a website with known vulnerabilities, and the results presented showcase the model’s ability to generate accurate and contextually relevant commands that successfully exploited the identified weaknesses.

title: Agentic Pipeline Operations: LLM Agents for CI/CD Failure Triage and Remediation under Human-in-the-Loop Guardrails
venue: International Journal of Research and Applied Innovations
abstract: Failed pipeline runs are a persistent tax on platform engineering teams. In our experience operating continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) for a large regulated financial-services enterprise, most failures are not novel: they fall into a small set of recurring categories such as dependency resolution errors, flaky tests, expired credentials, image pull and registry faults, exhausted namespace quotas, and drift between declared manifests and live cluster state. Each still interrupts an engineer, who must read logs, correlate recent changes, and apply a well-known fix. This paper proposes an agentic pipeline operations architecture in which a large language model (LLM) agent receives tool-scoped, mostly read-only access to pipeline logs, deployment manifests, run history, and repository history through the Model Context Protocol, a tool interface standard announced in late 2024. Actions are mediated by an autonomy gate that combines a per-action risk score with a calibrated confidence estimate to select one of five levels, from human-only operation to bounded auto-remediation of low-risk classes, and every decision is written to an append-only audit trail. On a replay corpus of 1,240 labelled failures reconstructed in a sandbox Kubernetes and Tekton environment, the agent reaches 87.6% top-1 triage accuracy against 57.1% for a rule-based matcher. Median time-to-green falls from 132 minutes under human-only handling to 30 minutes under bounded autonomy, and calibrated gating holds the auto-remediation false-remediation rate at 0.7%. We present the risk taxonomy, gate design, and practitioner guidance for introducing graded autonomy into regulated delivery platforms

title: AI at the Helm: End-to-End Invoice automation Using Pega GenAI and autonomous digital workers
venue: International Journal of Engineering in Computer Science
abstract: Revolutionizing invoice processing, this paper presents a next-generation intelligent automation framework powered by Pega GenAI Bots and Pega Robot Manager, delivering cognitive automation at enterprise scale. Traditional accounts payable systems are plagued by manual inefficiencies, diverse invoice layouts, and unstable ERP interfaces. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid solution that combines generative AI, large language models (LLMs), and hyper automation to construct a self-optimizing invoice pipeline. Leveraging OpenAI-driven data extraction through Pega’s Connect GenAI, the system interprets both structured and unstructured documents with high precision. Seamless orchestration of workflows is achieved via attended digital workers for exception handling and unattended RPA bots for fully automated invoice lifecycle management. Key innovations include real-time adaptability to legacy UI changes in systems like SAP, dynamic workflow coordination through Robot Manager, and self-healing mechanisms to mitigate AI hallucinations and UI drift. The framework was validated using a synthetic dataset of 1,000 varied invoice formats, achieving over 90% reduction in processing errors, 70% acceleration in cycle times, and 98% SLA compliance. Less than 10% of invoices required human intervention, indicating a high level of autonomy. Furthermore, performance remained consistent across different invoice types, including PO-based, utility, and scanned formats. These results demonstrate not only technical feasibility but also practical scalability, positioning the system as a robust solution for enterprise-wide deployment. By fusing AI reasoning with deterministic automation, the proposed architecture sets a new benchmark for AI-human collaboration in financial operations and provides a blueprint for trustworthy and resilient AI adoption in document-centric workflows.

title: AI-Augmented DevOps: Autonomous Software Delivery with Large Language Models
venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Engineering & Multidisciplinary Physical Sciences
abstract: The evolution of DevOps has accelerated software delivery through continuous integration, deployment, and infrastructure automation. However, modern systems' scale, dynamism, and complexity have outpaced traditional automation techniques. This paper introduces AI-augmented DevOps: an architectural and operational model that embeds intelligent agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) and machine learning into the DevOps lifecycle. We propose a modular five-layer framework consisting of observation, inference, action, feedback, and interaction layers, each designed to support autonomous, traceable, and policy-compliant decision-making. Our implementation leverages GPT-4 and reinforcement learning to enhance tasks such as log summarization, Infrastructure-As-Code (IaC) generation, and real-time incident remediation. A simulated CI/CD environment and real-world case studies demonstrate significant improvements in deployment frequency, MTTR, and change failure rates. The paper provides a blueprint for integrating AI into software delivery pipelines, enabling systems that continuously learn, adapt, and improve while maintaining human oversight and operational governance.

title: AI-Augmented Self-Healing Infrastructure: Combining Health Probes with Remediation Playbooks
venue: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management
abstract: Self-healing infrastructure has evolved as a foundational component in resilient, cloud-native systems. This paper introduces an advanced framework that enhances traditional health probe-driven remediation with artificial intelligence and machine learning. By integrating AI-powered anomaly detection, adaptive remediation strategies, and generative playbook synthesis, the proposed architecture transforms reactive fault response into a proactive, predictive, and autonomous paradigm. Utilizing native observability tools like Kubernetes, AWS CloudWatch, and Prometheus, combined with LLM-based pattern inference, we build a multi-tiered AI-driven monitoring system. Event-driven automation via AWS Lambda and EventBridge is extended with intelligent decision engines and reinforcement learning loops. Remediation workflows are executed through Ansible and AWS Systems Manager and enhanced by AI-generated playbooks tailored to novel incidents. Empirical validation shows dramatic reductions in MTTR, enhanced failure prevention rates, and lower operational overhead. This research redefines self-healing as an intelligent, continuously evolving capability vital for multi-cloud resilience. To our knowledge, this is the first framework to integrate LLMs and RL for playbook synthesis in self-healing cloud environments.

title: AI-Driven Self-Healing High-Frequency Trading (HFT) Infrastructure for Fault Prediction and Latency Optimization
venue: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
abstract: High-Frequency Trading (HFT) systems operate under extreme latency requirements, where microsecond deviations can result in significant financial impact. This paper introduces a cloud-native, agent-based self-healing infrastructure utilizing large language models (LLMs) for fault prediction and latency mitigation. Without the overhead of training bespoke machine learning models, pre-deployed LLM agents interpret structured telemetry streams—CPU load, network jitter, queue depth, and disk I/O—to generate actionable insights. These agents communicate with cloud services such as Azure Monitor, Open Telemetry, and Kubernetes to trigger automated failover and scaling actions. The architecture integrates FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) acceleration and kernel bypass technologies for deterministic low-latency processing. This approach yields a scalable, explainable, and operationally efficient framework for real-time fault recovery in HFT environments.

title: AI-Driven Trouble Ticket Generation and Misconfiguration Diagnosis in Enterprise Systems
abstract: Misconfigurations in enterprise IT systems remain a leading cause of service disruptions and vulnerabilities. In this paper, we present a self-adaptive AI agent that interactively collects diagnostic symptoms through natural language conversations and collaborates with an automated diagnosis system to identify root causes. The AI agent holds a dialog with the user to clarify the user complaint and then translates it into structured diagnostic tickets by mapping symptoms to relevant configuration variables (CVs) and assigning initial confidence scores. These tickets guide ConfExp, a confidence-driven diagnostic framework, which refines hypotheses through system-level test execution. The combined system significantly improves the diagnosis process. In evaluations across 75 fault scenarios in emulated enterprise environments, the system correctly identified misconfigured components in over 93% of cases while reducing the number of tests required by up to 47% compared to using ConfExp alone. This demonstrates the e ectiveness of combining a large language model (LLM)-driven symptom elicitation with confidence-guided test execution for scalable, automated troubleshooting.

title: AI for Threat Detection in Project Development
venue: University of Debrecen Electronic Archive (University of Debrecen)
abstract: This thesis presents the design and implementation of CloudNova, an AI-powered threat detection system developed to identify misconfigurations and potential security risks in cloud environments. The project integrates rule-based detection modules with a machine learning model to evaluate configuration files, logs, and cloud activity data. Using Python and the Flask framework, CloudNova analyzes uploaded inputs, predicts a security risk score through a trained Decision Tree Classifier, and generates structured reports in JSON and PDF formats. The system also includes an educational AI assistant that explains security concepts and a “CloudMind” generator that creates secure YAML configurations for services similar to AWS. Testing demonstrated that CloudNova effectively detects common misconfigurations and produces accurate risk evaluations in simulated environments. The results confirm that combining automation with artificial intelligence can enhance DevSecOps workflows, improve configuration security, and assist developers in preventing threats early in the project lifecycle. Future work includes integrating live cloud scanning, GPT-based assistance, and auto-remediation features.

title: AI-Powered Cloud Architecture, Agile Analytics, and Enterprise DevOps -Enabled Framework for Healthcare and Insurance Ecosystem Optimisation
venue: International Conference on Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics (ICONSTEM)
abstract: This framework introduces a transformative AI driven architecture based on GPT 4 powered intelligent automation and Azure machine learning pipelines to revolutionise healthcare insurance ecosystem interoperability. The solution merges the use of real time predictive analytics using TensorFlow-based neural networks for claims processing optimization resulting in a shortened approval process down by 73 %. Kubernetes orchestrated microservices to be deployed with CI/CD pipelines via Jenkins then gitops with 99.9 % availability of the system. NLP using BERT models is used in the framework for the automated interpretation of the medical records improving the diagnostic accuracy by 41 %. Apache Kafka makes it possible to stream data easily between Electronic Health Records (EHR) and insurances and MLOps workflows making it possible to update the existing model continuously. Security compliance, that meets HIPAA standards with audit trails created with blockchain technology activities. Performance evidence demonstrating Operational Expenditure 58% Patient Claim Reconciliation efficiency 65 % is established Startling Scalable FHIR compliant Healthcare Digitalization infrastructure of next generation.

title: An End-To-End LLM Enhanced Trading System
venue: Journal of Applied Business and Economics
abstract: This project introduces an end-to-end trading system that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) for real-time market sentiment analysis and trading signal generation. By synthesizing financial news and social-media streams, the system integrates sentiment-driven insights with technical indicators to support actionable investment decisions. FinGPT serves as the core sentiment model, ensuring domain-specific accuracy, while additional models validate performance across financial contexts. The framework combines live multi-source data processing, LLM-based summarization, and real-world strategy testing, deployed on Kubernetes for scalable operation. This comprehensive approach demonstrates how advanced LLM techniques can enhance trading strategies through timely and nuanced sentiment understanding.

title: An Enterprise-Scale Retrieval-Augmented Generative Intelligence Platform for Real-Time Financial Document Synthesis and Regulatory Compliance Automation
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence Data Science and Machine Learning
abstract: Financial services enterprises process vast volumes of unstructured documents-loan agreements, compliance filings, audit reports, and customer correspondence-requiring synthesis, summarization, and regulatory cross-referencing under strict accuracy and traceability constraints. Conventional document automation relies on rule-based extraction or single-pass large language model (LLM) summarization, both of which struggle with provenance tracking, multi-document reasoning, and auditability demanded by financial regulators. This paper presents the Enterprise Generative Document Intelligence Platform (EGDIP), a layered system architecture integrating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), microservices-based orchestration, and containerized deployment to deliver scalable, traceable document synthesis for regulated financial environments. EGDIP organizes processing into four cooperating layers: a data ingestion layer supporting heterogeneous document formats and streaming updates, a retrieval and indexing layer built on vector-based semantic search, an intelligence layer combining a fine-tuned LLM with deterministic compliance-rule validation, and a consumption layer exposing synthesized outputs through RESTful APIs and interactive dashboards. The system was deployed on a containerized Kubernetes environment and evaluated on a corpus of 180,000 financial documents from loan servicing and regulatory filing workflows. Results show a 58.3% reduction in document review time, a 39.7% improvement in cross-reference accuracy relative to keyword-based retrieval baselines, and sub-second retrieval latency at the evaluated scale. These findings demonstrate that combining retrieval-augmented generation with deterministic validation yields a practical, auditable path toward generative AI adoption in compliance-sensitive enterprise settings.

title: Anomaly Detection and Root Cause Analysis in Cloud-Native Environments Using Large Language Models and Bayesian Networks
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Cloud computing technologies offer significant advantages in scalability and performance, enabling rapid deployment of applications. The adoption of microservices-oriented architectures has introduced an ecosystem characterized by an increased number of applications, frameworks, abstraction layers, orchestrators, and hypervisors, all operating within distributed systems. This complexity results in the generation of vast quantities of logs from diverse sources, making the analysis of these events an inherently challenging task, particularly in the absence of automation. To address this issue, Machine Learning techniques leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising approach for dynamically identifying patterns within these events. In this study, we propose a novel anomaly detection framework utilizing a microservices architecture deployed on Kubernetes and Istio, enhanced by an LLM model. The model was trained on various error scenarios, with Chaos Mesh employed as an error injection tool to simulate faults of different natures, and Locust used as a load generator to create workload stress conditions. After an anomaly is detected by the LLM model, we employ a dynamic Bayesian network to provide probabilistic inferences about the incident, proving the relationships between components and assessing the degree of impact among them. Additionally, a ChatBot powered by the same LLM model allows users to interact with the AI, ask questions about the detected incident, and gain deeper insights. The experimental results demonstrated the model's effectiveness, reliably identifying all error events across various test scenarios. While it successfully avoided missing any anomalies, it did produce some false positives, which remain within acceptable limits.

title: APPLICATION OF LARGESCALE LANGUAGE MODELS FOR INTELLIGENT CONTROL OF KUBERNETES CLUSTERS: POSSIBILITIES AND PROSPECTS
venue: SOFT MEASUREMENTS AND COMPUTING
abstract: This article examines the main approaches to integrating large language models (LLMs) into container orchestration management systems such as Kubernetes. The potential of LLMs for automating operational tasks is analyzed, including the generation of YAML manifests, optimization of resource requests/limits, and incident diagnostics. A threetier architecture of an intelligent assistant is proposed, comprising an interface layer for natural language processing, a processing layer with RAGbased context enrichment mechanisms, and an execution layer for interacting with the Kubernetes API. The article also discusses limitations related to security (prompt injection, data leakage) and reliability (hallucinations, API dependencies). Promising directions are identified, such as the development of domainspecific models, multimodal metric analysis, creation of autonomous agents based on reinforcement learning, and an assessment of potential levels of LLM integration into the orchestrator.

title: Architecting Next-Gen Financial Systems with AI and Cloud-Native Microservice
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Architecting Next-Gen Financial Systems with AI and Cloud-Native Microservice Conference: Conference: 4th IEEE World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC-2025) IEEE Conference ID: 66080 Frameworks for designing financial systems combining AI models and cloud-native microservices • Reference architectures integrating Large Language Models (LLMs), vector databases, Kafka-based real-time ingestion, and zero-trust security patterns • Use cases spanning revenue automation, AML surveillance, ESG scoring, and investment operations optimization • LLM-powered components embedded into microservices using frameworks such as LangChain and Kubernetes • Real-time data federation through Kafka streams and vector embeddings • Workflow automation using ServiceNow integrated with AI decision engines • Compliance enforcement using containerized audit logs and policy-as-code mechanisms Referenced: Mastering AI & Machine Learning in ServiceNow: Intelligent Automation & Data-Driven Solutions Author: Sasibhushan Rao Chanthati (ISBN: 978-89704-145-9) The accelerating pace of digital transformation in the financial services industry demands a redefinition of enterprise infrastructure to enable real-time responsiveness, compliance, and intelligent decision-making. This paper presents a framework for designing next-generation financial systems by combining AI models with cloud-native microservices and secure workflow orchestration. Leveraging scholarly contributions to IEEE journals, the author introduces a modular reference architecture that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), vector databases, Kafka-based real-time ingestion, and zero-trust security patterns. Use cases span revenue automation, AML surveillance, ESG scoring, and investment operations optimization.
